Solution (a) Because the reaction is first order in H PO , 2 2 2( ) aq tripling this concentration will tri­ ple the reaction rate.

Rate expressions that depend on more than one concentration are more difficult to obtain experimentally than those that depend just on one. One method is to find the instantaneous initial rates of reaction for several values of one of the concentra­ tions, holding the other initial concentrations fixed from one run to the next. The experiment can then be repeated, changing one of the other concentrations. The following example illustrates this procedure.
